title: Name what kind of change a roster made

blocks.text: The line-maintenance group's golden test (practice 1) now says *what* changed, but a reviewer still has to decide *what kind* of change it is before deciding what to do. Write the triage.
The docstring of `triage.py` gives a record's shape. The roster model **minimizes** cost. Write `classify(expected, actual)`, returning one word:

items: `"input"` when the two records were solved from different data (their `input` hashes differ); nothing else about them can be compared, so this answer wins over every other;
`"better"` or `"worse"` when the costs differ by more than `COST_TOLERANCE` dollars, by which way the cost moved;
`"tie"` when the costs are the same within the tolerance but the assignments differ: another roster of equal cost;
`"same"` when nothing differs beyond the tolerance.

blocks.text:
"""Say what kind of change separates a crew-roster result from its golden record.

A record is a dict:
    "input":  the content hash of the data the roster was solved from
    "status": the solver's termination, e.g. "OPTIMAL"
    "cost":   the roster's cost in dollars; the model minimizes it
    "assign": {job: crew}
"""

from __future__ import annotations

COST_TOLERANCE = 1.0   # dollars


def classify(expected: dict, actual: dict) -> str:
    """One of "input", "status", "better", "worse", "tie" or "same"."""
    # TODO: check the causes in the right order.
    return "same"

if __name__ == "__main__":
    golden = {"input": "9f2c", "status": "OPTIMAL", "cost": 980.0, "assign": {"j1": "red"}}
    print(classify(golden, {**golden, "cost": 940.0}))

cases.says: an unchanged record is "same", and a record from other input data is "input"
the model minimizes cost, so a lower cost is "better" and a higher one "worse"
a cost within the tolerance with different assignments is a "tie", not a better or worse roster
when the input and the status both changed, the input explains the rest, so the answer is "input"
